title: The Ledger of Saint Alder's Revisited
premise: Insurance investigator Casper Eriksen is hired by an elderly woman to prove that her brother, declared dead thirty years ago, was never murdered — a strange request until he learns the 'victim' was recently seen alive in Saint Alder's, and the original death certificate was the linchpin of a fraud that made several townspeople wealthy. Using his photographic memory of archived documents, Casper reconstructs the night of the supposed murder, discovering the brother faked his death to escape a corrupt mill owner and that the client herself helped bury the truth. As the old conspirators close ranks — one dies suspiciously before Casper can interview him — he realizes the client's real goal is not vindication but a deathbed confession before the last witness, the brother himself, succumbs to illness. In the end, Casper must choose between closing the case cleanly or exposing a survival built on a lie, and he chooses mercy: he files a report proving the murder never happened, while privately returning the brother's true ledger to him, letting memory — not the law — settle the debt.
about_author: Wren Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records in small coastal towns, where every filing cabinet seemed to hide a second story. They write quiet, document-driven mysteries about people whose pasts refuse to stay filed.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV: Casper Eriksen. A frail client, Maren Voss, pays triple rate to prove her brother Torben's 1994 murder never happened — no killer, no body, only a certificate. Casper, unsettled by the inversion of his trade, pulls the original claim file and recognizes a forged signature he's seen once before. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into unease as the case opens backward.

chapters.title: The Mill's Quiet Partners
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. In Saint Alder's, Casper interviews the beneficiaries of Torben's life insurance — now the town's mill owners and councilmen — whose alibis are polished, rehearsed, thirty years too smooth. His photographic memory flags that two depositions use identical phrasing. That night someone ransacks his hotel room, searching for something he doesn't yet know he has. Emotional beat: the town's charm revealing its teeth.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Following a discrepancy in the tide records, Casper finds Torben's hidden ledger in a boathouse — proof the 'murder' was staged to flee mill owner Halvard Brane, who was laundering money through the death claim. Before Casper can confront him, Brane dies of 'heart failure,' and Maren admits she helped stage the death to save her brother. Emotional beat: the case's moral floor giving way beneath him.

chapters.title: The Closing Entry
chapters.summary: POV: Casper, with a final letter from Torben. The dying conspirators close in to destroy the ledger, forcing Casper into a standoff at the flooded mill where it all began; he trades the ledger's public exposure for Maren's signed confession and Torben's freedom. He files his report: no murder, ever. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, and memory — not justice — carrying the truth forward.
